name: Frase
summary: AI-powered SEO content writing and optimization. Research, outline, write, and optimize articles that rank — all in one place.
best_for: content teams and SEOs who want to speed up research, briefs and SERP-driven optimization in one workflow
skip_if: you publish only occasionally — the monthly quota and subscription outweigh the time saved for a handful of articles
honest_knock: The article quotas pinch if you publish at volume (overage docs bill each), and it's a research-and-optimization tool, not a magic ranking button — it speeds up briefs, it doesn't replace the writing or the backlinks. In our test on 20 October 2026 the writer put back a claim we had rejected, now credited to the National Institutes of Health, and ignored our audience and 'no product tips' instructions, so every generated article needs a human check on its claims.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month billed yearly ($49 monthly), 1 seat, 1 site
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-21 against Frase's own machine-readable pricing file frase.io/pricing.md; every plan price below was unchanged from our 17 August, 14 September and 3 October readings) The headline figure is the yearly rate; paying month to month costs about 25% more, and both are shown on the page. Starter $39/mo billed yearly against $49/mo monthly: 1 seat, 1 site, 10 articles and 50 audit pages a month, Content Guard watching 10 pages. Professional $103/mo yearly against $129/mo monthly: 3 seats, 5 sites, 40 articles and 250 audit pages, extra seats $29/mo. Scale $239/mo yearly against $299/mo monthly: 5 seats, up to 10 domains, 100 articles and 1,000 audit pages, Content Guard watching 300 pages, extra seats $29/mo. The trial is 7 days with no credit card. FraseCMS hosting is included free up to 100,000 page views a month; Basic at $19/mo on top of a paid plan raises that to 250,000, drops the Frase badge and lets the blog sit on your own domain or a subdirectory, and Pro is $99/mo at a million page views, with $1.00 and $0.50 per extra 1,000 page views and a spend cap set at the base price by default. On Starter, Frase stops at the limit rather than billing you extra; on Professional and Scale you can switch on pay-as-you-go capacity, so there the sticker price is a floor rather than a ceiling: Professional adds $5 per extra article, $0.50 per audit page and $0.25 per AI prompt, Scale $4, $0.40 and $0.20. API, MCP and CLI requests are capped at 5,000, 20,000 and 50,000 a month on the three self-serve plans. Every plan also tracks how AI answers mention your brand (Frase calls it AI Visibility), daily and with alerts: Starter covers ChatGPT and Google AI, Professional adds Perplexity, and Scale adds Claude and Gemini (pricing and feature pages read 21 October 2026). How many prompts each plan tracks for this is not stated.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the 7-day trial, with no card asked: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We asked Frase for one article on 'how to organize a reusable packing checklist' for individual travellers, with three sections, no product tips, no prices and no invented statistics; we checked its key facts, rejected one claim, let it write, and looked at the score and the export options.
findings: A site is required. Without one Frase said 'No sites configured. Add a site first to create content bound to it.' Adding our domain asked for no verification, and the website analysis could be skipped.

The brief overrode our instructions. Frase replaced our audience with 'Shopify Merchants, GTM Leaders, SaaS Operations Managers, Business Travelers', taken from the linked site, planned five sections instead of three, and added a step 'Select an Editable Packing Checklist Tool' with '3 tool recommendations'.

Its own source check worked: it marked a PubMed claim about working memory load as 'not on the page'. The outline still listed that claim as 'EVIDENCE TO INCLUDE - STAT, Source: National Institutes of Health'. We rejected it, and Frase then said it 'will not be claimed'.
The rejected claim appeared in the article anyway, now credited to the National Institutes of Health. Frase wrote the 935-word article in about a minute and a half.

The article also named five products (Todoist, Asana, Notion, Airtable, PackPoint) despite our 'no product recommendations', and used a business setting (trade show, booth, business cards) for an audience of individual travellers. It contained no percentages or prices.
One article took the trial counter from 5 to 4 articles. The editor scored the draft 64, with 4 of 5 sections, 80% coverage, 0 links and 0 images.

Export in the trial covers HTML, PDF, Markdown and plain text downloads, Notion and Google Docs, plus 'Repurpose Content' for LinkedIn and Instagram carousels, an X thread and a newsletter. We did not download anything.

vendor_mcp.what: Server shipped as the @frase/mcp-server npm package: analyse the live SERP, run a competitor gap, build the brief, draft and score the page for SEO and GEO, audit a domain, read back AI-visibility and Search Console data, and publish to WordPress, Webflow, Sanity, Wix or FraseCMS once you approve.
vendor_mcp.plan: Included with Frase, from $39 a month billed yearly. Their words: "There is no separate add-on." Activity through the server counts against the same plan limits as the app — the briefs, audits and content you already pay for. A 7-day trial, no card.
